hypothesis: The measured 128-thread mappings with two and four targets per thread were both slower than the baseline, and the factor-four trial was slower than factor two. Keeping two targets per thread but using 256 threads per block with 512 targets per block tests whether more lanes and fewer targets per thread help at the same per-block target coverage as the factor-four mapping. Register pressure and block-level parallelism may still limit performance; no speedup is assumed.
notes: Candidate only; no correctness or performance measurements are claimed. The mapping uses two distinct targets per thread at offsets 0 and blockDim.x, with 512 targets per block, guards each partial target independently, reuses each source position and mass across valid target calculations, and uses no shared memory. Request the controller's full correctness checks and official scored-size measurements.
transformations: Map each thread to two distinct targets at blockIdx.x*(2*blockDim.x)+threadIdx.x and that index plus blockDim.x; guard the targets independently for partial groups.
Load each source position and mass once per source iteration and reuse them across the valid target calculations in registers; keep each target's accumulators separate.
Write each valid target exactly once and use no shared-memory source tiling or block-level multi-output assignment.
